definitions.gloss: ill will; bad feeling; animosity; hostility
definitions.explanation: Negative feelings toward someone, such as resentment, hostility, or dislike. Describes a persistent emotional attitude rather than a temporary mood.

examples.japanese: {悪感情|あくかんじょう}を{抱|いだ}く。
{彼|かれ}に{対|たい}して{悪感情|あくかんじょう}はない。
examples.english: I have no ill feelings toward him.

examples.japanese: あの{発言|はつげん}が{原因|げんいん}で、{二人|ふたり}の{間|あいだ}に{悪感情|あくかんじょう}が{生|う}まれた。
examples.english: That remark caused bad feelings between the two of them.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{悪感情|あくかんじょう}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えて、ようやく{和解|わかい}することができた。
examples.english: They were finally able to reconcile after overcoming years of animosity.

notes:
Composed of {悪|あく} (bad, evil) and {感情|かんじょう} (feeling, emotion). A straightforward compound describing negative interpersonal feelings. Often appears in formal or written contexts when discussing relationships or conflicts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {悪感情|あくかんじょう}を{抱|いだ}く: to harbor ill will
- {悪感情|あくかんじょう}が{生|う}まれる: for bad feelings to arise
- {悪感情|あくかんじょう}はない: to have no ill will
- {悪感情|あくかんじょう}を{持|も}つ: to have bad feelings

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {敵意|てきい}: hostility, enmity — stronger; implies active opposition or antagonism
- {反感|はんかん}: antipathy, aversion — focuses on instinctive dislike or opposition
- {悪意|あくい}: malice, ill intent — implies deliberate intention to harm, not just negative feelings
